summary: Round r1 (restricted network). For Q1 (climate finance Nepal has accessed from GCF, GEF and MDBs versus approved) the structure of the answer is defined in specific.climate_finance_access: eight channels (GCF, GEF/LDCF/SCCF, Adaptation Fund, CIF, World Bank, ADB, OECD all-provider climate-related development finance, and MoF on-budget climate expenditure) each with approved, committed, disbursed, access ratio, grant share and adaptation share, plus NDC/NAP need-side figures. All values are pending. Only one lead (GCF portfolio, carried from 16A) was found by search; the remaining fund-portal URLs are from the source catalog or general knowledge and are marked unverified because the web search budget was exhausted before 25D searches and all fund hosts are blocked. Main methodological risks: double counting across funds channelled via MDBs, attribution of multi-country projects, Rio-marker over-attribution, and mismatched period bases (calendar, World Bank FY, Nepal FY).

findings.claim: Q1: Climate finance approved for Nepal by GCF, GEF (incl. LDCF/SCCF), Adaptation Fund, CIF, World Bank and ADB, cumulative to latest cut-off.
findings.period: cumulative to a common cut-off date (to be set on retrieval)

findings.claim: Q1: Climate finance disbursed (accessed) to Nepal by the same channels, and access ratio disbursed/approved per channel.
findings.note: Disbursement fields on GCF project pages, GEF database, WB/ADB project pages.

findings.claim: All-provider climate-related development finance to Nepal (OECD CRS, Rio markers), commitments vs disbursements.
findings.note: Lead 25D-L04; convert to Nepal FY only via transaction-level dates.

findings.claim: Nepal's stated climate finance needs (NDC, NAP) for the access-vs-need comparison.
findings.note: Lead 25D-L11 (UNFCCC NDC registry; catalog lacks a UNFCCC id).

findings.claim: Access is measured as cumulative disbursement over cumulative approval per channel at a common cut-off date; multi-country projects are included only for stated Nepal allocations; funds flowing via MDBs (CIF, GCF co-financing) are netted to avoid double counting.
MDB climate finance is reported as the climate co-benefit share of project commitments per joint MDB methodology and kept separate from dedicated climate-fund flows.

data_gaps: No values retrieved; all fund portals blocked.
Only one fund lead found by search (GCF root, via 16A); other URLs unverified.
Nepal allocations within multi-country GCF/GEF projects may not be published.
MoF Development Cooperation Report and climate budget code documents for FY2023/24-FY2025/26 not located as direct files.
Source catalog lacks ids for Adaptation Fund, CIF, UNFCCC and Climate Funds Update (academic used as proxy).

assumptions.text: USD current prices are the reporting unit for fund flows; NPR conversions use NRB exchange rates at transaction dates and are labelled.
Loans and grants are reported separately; loan-financed climate finance also enters external debt (Agent 26E), so it is not added to grants in the model's grants variable.
Approval is not access; scenario inputs for external financing (X24) use disbursement paths, not approvals.

challenges.text: Coordinate on X24: ODA totals from OECD/MoF include climate-related flows; 25D will supply the climate component with a double-counting reconciliation, not an additive series.
MDB climate loans add to external public debt; please flag concessional terms so the debt module does not treat them as grants.
channels.py external_financing owners omit 25D (as 16A itself noted); 25D confirms it supplies the climate-finance component of X24.
Request catalog ids for adaptation_fund, cif, unfccc and climate_funds_update, and confirmation of the GCF and GEF country-page URLs on first fetch.

uncertainty: High. No values retrieved. Structural uncertainty from attribution of multi-country projects, co-benefit accounting in MDB portfolios, Rio-marker coding, and disbursement reporting lags (disbursement data are often reported with a lag of a year or more relative to approvals). Period bases differ across sources (calendar, World Bank FY, Nepal FY).

definitions.approved: Board/Council approval of financing attributed to Nepal (single-country projects fully; multi-country projects only where the Nepal allocation is stated)
definitions.committed: Legal agreement signed/effective (MDB commitment; GCF FAA effectiveness)
definitions.disbursed: Cumulative transfers to the executing/implementing entity or recipient to the cut-off date
definitions.access_ratio: disbursed divided by approved, computed per channel with matching cut-off dates

by_channel.channel: Green Climate Fund (funded projects and readiness)
by_channel.period_basis: calendar (Board approval dates); convert to Nepal FY via transaction dates
by_channel.notes: Multi-country programmes must not be attributed fully to Nepal; record accredited entity (international vs direct access)

by_channel.period_basis: GEF replenishment period and calendar approval dates
by_channel.notes: LDCF is GEF-managed but separate; GEF grant and co-financing kept separate
Channelled through MDBs; avoid double counting with CF-05/CF-06

by_channel.period_basis: World Bank FY (July-June) - differs from Nepal FY and calendar
by_channel.notes: Climate co-benefit share is a methodology-based attribution, not a separate flow
Joint MDB climate finance methodology; adaptation/mitigation split

by_channel.channel: Bilateral and all-provider climate-related development finance (OECD)
by_channel.notes: Rio-marker 'significant' flows overstate climate finance if counted fully; report principal and significant separately

by_channel.channel: Nepal on-budget climate-relevant expenditure and receipts (MoF)
by_channel.notes: Climate budget code covers domestic and foreign-financed spending; not a measure of access alone

access_constraints_to_assess: number and type of accredited entities based in Nepal (direct access)
project preparation capacity and readiness support
MDB loan vs grant terms and debt implications (link to 26E)
fiduciary and procurement delays (link to domestic Agent 03)
